title: DECLARE ... CURSOR FOR EXECUTE 在同名 portal 关闭后重用，portal 类型未交叉核对。上游在此报错，17.5 接受
live_proof: CVE-2026-16239, fixed upstream in 60887d34818a, which postdates the 17.5 pin
fidelity: real server. Not reached under the single-user backend: DECLARE CURSOR requires a transaction block and postgres --single has no implicit one. Reaching it needs a postmaster and an extended-query-protocol client, so the arms record a harness limit rather than a verdict

spatial.precondition: PGSU_NESTED=none. needs the Capstone application VM: a case is SQL run against a real postgres process, not a freestanding domain. Every attempt needs a fresh copy of a cluster made by the 16-byte-MAXALIGN backend (app/build-native16-fixture.py); an ordinary 8-byte native cluster is not interchangeable. Set CAPSTONE_REV_NODES=262144: this workload exhausts the 65536 default and passes at 262144 with a high-water mark of 84193 nodes (capstone/ports/common/application/README.md lines 36-37; the measurement is nodes_high_water in ports/common/application/results/20260929-delegation.json). Scoring: node exhaustion is a resource limit, not a detection -- it surfaces as cause 30 (RISCV_EXCP_INSUF_RESOURCES = 0x1e, capstone-qemu/target/riscv/cpu_bits.h), so an oracle that counts faults will score it as a catch. Record causes by name: the emulator and the RTL number them differently (ports/nginx/e1-bundle/e1-bundle.py:151). Also: su can return 0 after a child SIGPROT, so exit status alone does not qualify a run; the adapter report has to agree.
